channel.title: Butch Mahinay
channel.description: New blog posts and Python for Treasury Work lessons by Butch Mahinay

item.title: Lesson 7: Keep a receipts register in SQLite
item.description: Save official receipts in a small database file, total them with SQL, and let the database itself refuse a duplicate OR number.

item.title: Data Analytics Series, Part 1: What Data Analytics Really Is, and Why Every Office Already Has the Data
item.description: Data analytics is the craft of turning everyday records into answers people can act on. Here is what it means, the four kinds of questions it can answer, a famous cholera map from 1854, and why a local treasury is already sitting on a mountain of useful data.

item.title: Project Management Series, Part 1: The Accidental Project Manager in the Treasury
item.description: Nobody in a local treasury applies to be a project manager, yet many of us end up as one. Here is how a project differs from daily work, the three limits every project lives with, and four moves to make in your first two weeks.

item.title: Lesson 6: Make a formatted Excel report with openpyxl
item.description: Turn the day's receipts into a real Excel file with a bold header, peso formatting, a SUM formula and a frozen top row.

item.title: Year-End in the Treasury: What Really Happens in December
item.description: While most offices slow down for Christmas, the local treasury speeds up. Here is what happens in December, from bonuses and last-minute vouchers to unspent budgets, cash counts and getting ready for the January rush.

item.title: Your Data at the Treasury Counter: What an Office May Share, and What It Must Protect
item.description: Every payment at the town hall leaves a trail of personal information. Here is what the Data Privacy Act means at the treasury counter, what an office may share, what it must protect, and simple habits that keep taxpayers safe.

item.title: Cybersecurity Series, Part 1: How Modern Cyberattacks Really Work
item.description: Forget the hoodie-wearing genius. Today's cyberattacks are run like businesses. Learn what security protects, who the attackers are, how a breach unfolds step by step, and why layered defenses work.

item.title: How to Use the RPT Calculator: Know Your Amilyar Before You Pay
item.description: A step-by-step guide to the free Real Property Tax Calculator on this site, with worked examples, and the lessons every property owner should know about discounts, interest and where the money goes.

item.title: Lesson 2: Check an official receipt series for gaps and duplicates
item.description: Compare the receipts recorded today with the booklet issued, and flag missing, repeated or stray numbers.

item.title: Lesson 3: Compute real property tax penalties with Decimal
item.description: See why floats are unsafe for money, then compute 2% monthly penalties with a 36-month cap, rounded correctly.

item.title: Lesson 4: Build a simple RCD summary with pandas
item.description: Group collections by collector and fund, list the receipts used, and match collections against deposits.

item.title: Lesson 5: Make a tamper-evident log with HMAC
item.description: Seal each log entry with a keyed hash chained to the one before it, so any later edit or deletion shows.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 3: Every Document Has an Owner
item.description: A receipt that belongs to everyone belongs to no one. Every form in custody and every peso in hand needs a named, bonded officer who answers for it.

item.title: Lesson 1: Add up a day's collections from a CSV file
item.description: Read the day's official receipts from a spreadsheet export and total them per fund, to the centavo.

item.title: So Close to Alibijaban Island
item.description: On Hermano Puli Day, I sat alone on someone else's bangka in San Andres, Quezon, and looked out at an island I have loved for almost two decades. This time, I could not cross.

item.title: Why .dev and Not .com: How I Chose My Website's Address
item.description: Most people expect a .com. I chose aumahinay.dev. Here is why, in plain words, and what it taught me about building things that are safe by default.

item.title: 200 Kilometers and Five Years Later: Coming Home to the Farm
item.description: Five years. That is how long it had been since I last set foot on my 3-hectare farm.

item.title: Lesson 0: Getting started: install Python and run your first script
item.description: Install Python on Windows or Mac, open the command line, and run a script, with fixes for the usual first errors.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 2: Every Peso Has a Document
item.description: No collection without an accountable form, no release without a voucher. A peso that leaves no paper behind cannot be accounted for.

item.title: 360 Degrees: My First Post as Acting Municipal Treasurer
item.description: Two years, two Mayors, a pandemic, a typhoon and an election: what my first post as Acting Municipal Treasurer of Mulanay, Quezon, taught me.

item.title: The ALTOS Framework, Principle 1: Legality First
item.description: Before we ask how a peso was handled, we should ask whether the law allowed it at all.

item.title: Why I Built ALTOS: Bringing Automation to Philippine Local Treasuries
item.description: A treasury system built around one idea: every peso should be accounted for from the moment it arrives to the moment it is reported.
